examFormat.rulesSummary: 2025–2027 syllabus · Core · scientific calculator required; no algebraic/graphical calculator · formula facts included · original full-length practice

title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) · Paper 3 — original full-length mock (calculator)
subject: cambridge-igcse-mathematics-0580
instructions: Original full-length practice: 24 questions, 80 marks. This is not an official or endorsed Cambridge examination. Answer every question and all parts. Show your reasoning and calculations in the working canvas beneath each question; add pages when needed. A scientific calculator is required; algebraic and graphical calculators are not permitted. Retain unrounded values during calculations. Unless a question specifies otherwise, give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures and angles in degrees to one decimal place. Use the calculator value of π or 3.142. Formula facts are attached to every question. Draw and label your own axes where requested; one grid square may represent the scale stated in the question. Use straight ruled lines and smooth curves as appropriate. Dimensions stated in a question are exact unless described as rounded. There is no separate reading period.

resources.label: Core formula facts
resources.text:
Mathematical formula facts — independently typeset for this practice paper
Triangle: area = bh/2 (b is the base, h the perpendicular height).
Circle: area = πr²; circumference = 2πr (r is the radius).
Cylinder: curved surface area = 2πrh; volume = πr²h.
Cone: curved surface area = πrl; volume = πr²h/3 (l is slant height; h is perpendicular height).
Sphere: surface area = 4πr²; volume = 4πr³/3.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Pyramid: volume = base area × perpendicular height / 3.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt:
(a) Calculate (7.84² − 3.19)/2.6. Give your answer to three significant figures. [2]
(b) Round 0.006784 to two significant figures. [1]

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: $1800 is invested for three years at 4.2% compound interest per year. No money is added or withdrawn. Calculate the interest earned after three years, to the nearest cent. [3]

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt:
A metal block has volume 18.6 cm³ and mass 145.08 g. Density = mass ÷ volume.
(a) Find the density of the metal. [2]
(b) Find the mass of a 25 cm³ block of the same metal. [1]

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt: A spacecraft travels 4.86 × 10⁷ km in 1.35 × 10⁵ seconds. Calculate its average speed in km/s, giving the answer in standard form. [3]

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt:
A container holds V litres, recorded as 3.8 litres to the nearest 0.1 litre.
(a) Write the error interval for V. [2]
(b) Convert the recorded volume of 3.8 litres to cm³. [1]

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt:
The formula C = 5(F − 32)/9 connects two temperature scales.
(a) Calculate C when F = 95. [1]
(b) Make F the subject of the formula. [2]

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt: A taxi fare is a fixed charge of $3.20 plus $1.85 for every kilometre travelled. A passenger pays $25.40. Form an equation and calculate the distance travelled. [3]

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Two notebooks and three pens cost $10.10. Three notebooks and one pen cost $10.60. Find the price of one notebook and one pen. [3]

questions.label: Question 9
questions.prompt:
Line L has equation y = 3x − 4.
(a) State its gradient. [1]
(b) Find the equation of the line parallel to L that passes through (2,7). [2]

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt:
Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°.
(a) Calculate each exterior angle. [1]
(b) Find the number of sides of the polygon. Show your method. [2]

questions.label: Question 11
questions.prompt:
An open cylindrical container has internal radius 4.2 cm and height 11 cm. Ignore its wall thickness.
(a) Calculate its capacity in millilitres. [2]
(b) Calculate the area of material needed for its curved side and its circular base. [2]

questions.label: Question 12
questions.prompt:
A ramp rises 1.35 m above horizontal ground over a horizontal distance of 6.2 m.
(a) Calculate the length of the sloping ramp. [2]
(b) Calculate the angle it makes with the horizontal. [2]

questions.label: Question 13
questions.prompt:
A map has scale 1:25000. The straight-line distance from a station A to a school B measures 7.6 cm on the map. The bearing of B from A is 068°.
(a) Calculate the actual distance in kilometres. [2]
(b) State the bearing of A from B. [1]
(c) A park C is due south of A. State the bearing of C from A. [1]

questions.label: Question 14
questions.prompt:
The function is y = x² − 2x − 3.
(a) Make a table for x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. [1]
(b) Draw the graph on a square grid, using one square for one unit on each axis. [2]
(c) Use the graph to solve x² − 2x − 3 = 0. [1]

questions.label: Question 15
questions.prompt:
The number of bicycles owned by each of 30 households is recorded below.
Bicycles: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
Frequency: 4, 9, 10, 5, 2
(a) Find the modal number of bicycles. [1]
(b) Find the median. [1]
(c) Calculate the mean. [2]

questions.label: Question 16
questions.prompt:
Six households record the number of people and daily water use.
People x: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
Water y (litres): 85, 155, 205, 300, 345, 430
(a) Draw a scatter diagram: use x from 0 to 7 and y from 0 to 500, with clearly labelled uniform scales. [2]
(b) Describe the correlation. [1]
(c) Draw a line of best fit by eye and use it to estimate daily water use for a household of 4.5 people on average. [1]

questions.label: Question 17
questions.prompt:
A bag contains 4 yellow and 6 black counters. A counter is chosen at random, its colour recorded, and it is replaced. A second counter is then chosen at random.
(a) Draw a probability tree with probabilities on every branch. [2]
(b) Find the probability that both counters are yellow. [1]
(c) Find the probability that the two counters have different colours. [1]

questions.label: Question 18
questions.prompt:
A walker leaves home at 0900 and walks directly away from home at a constant speed. At 0930 she is 2 km from home, then rests there until 0945. She walks directly home at a constant speed and arrives at 1015.
(a) Draw the distance-from-home against time graph from 0900 to 1015. [2]
(b) Find her speed on the outward walk. [1]
(c) Calculate her average speed for the complete journey, including the rest. [1]

questions.label: Question 19
questions.prompt:
Triangle PQR has P(2,2), Q(6,2), R(2,4).
(a) Enlarge it by scale factor ½ with centre the origin. Draw and label the image on a coordinate grid. [3]
(b) State the scale factor of the enlargement that maps this image back to the original triangle. [1]

questions.label: Question 20
questions.prompt:
Of 40 students, 23 play football, 18 play basketball and 9 play both.
(a) Draw a two-circle Venn diagram and put the number of students in each of its four regions. [3]
(b) A student is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student plays exactly one of these sports. [1]

questions.label: Question 21
questions.prompt: A traveller exchanges $450 into euros. The rate is €0.92 for $1. The exchange office first deducts a fee of 2% of the dollar amount, then converts the remaining dollars. Calculate the euros received. [3]

questions.label: Question 22
questions.prompt:
A closed cuboid measures 6 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
(a) Sketch a valid net and label the dimensions of each rectangular face. The sketch need not be to scale. [2]
(b) Calculate its total surface area. [1]

questions.label: Question 23
questions.prompt:
A line touches a circle at T. O is the centre.
(a) State the angle between OT and the tangent at T. [1]
(b) Give the geometrical reason for your answer. [1]

questions.label: Question 24
questions.prompt: A shop increases a price by 20%, then reduces the new price by 20%. A customer says the final price equals the original price. Decide whether the customer is correct and justify your answer using multipliers or a numerical example. [2]
